title: Pre-Analysis Review — Proposed Extension of the Continuous Wall Wash Strip Beyond the Launch Operators

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: Closed review of a proposal to extend the continuous LED wall wash standard beyond its three launch operators; the extension was rejected on ceiling void clearance and on the cabin feeder margin that a seat power change has already claimed.

sections.objective: Decide whether the continuous LED wall wash standard should be extended from its three launch operators to the rest of the fleet, and establish what the extension would cost in clearance, feeder margin and bulletin terms. The review was raised internally after a fourth operator asked to take the standard at its next cabin refresh and the sales organisation asked for a fleet-wide position rather than a case by case one.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and the extension was rejected. The strip runs the length of the ceiling void that the treated air distribution risers also occupy, and on aircraft carrying the absorber inserts the clearance to the strip carrier falls below the installation rule over the wing. That is most of the population the extension was aimed at. Separately, the strip draws its supply from the aft cabin feeders whose remaining margin has already been claimed by the higher rated in-seat power supply now in pre-analysis, and the two changes were being planned against the same number by different offices. The bulletin is written per operator and cannot carry a fleet effectivity as it stands.
sections.next_steps: Reject the extension in its present form and tell the requesting operator directly rather than through the bulletin. Re-open it only when the seat power allocation is settled and a strip carrier with a lower profile is available for aircraft carrying the acoustic inserts. Keep the standard available to the three launch operators unchanged, and record the clearance case so the next request does not start from nothing.

remaining electrical margin on the aft cabin feeders

tasks.title: Measure the ceiling void clearance on treated riser aircraft
Check the aft cabin feeder margin against other claims
Assess whether the bulletin can carry a fleet effectivity

expected_findings.rationale: The strip carrier runs through the same ceiling void as the acoustically treated risers. On a treated duct the clearance to the carrier falls below the installation rule over the wing, and that population is most of the fleet the extension was aimed at.
expected_findings.resolution: Extension rejected until a lower profile carrier exists; the clearance case recorded for the next request.

evidence.similarity_note: No identifier in common: the two documents share neither a part number, a functional item number nor a zone. They were connected only by the language of aft cabin supply margin and turnaround load, and by the fact that both claim it.

expected_findings.rationale: The strip draws from the aft cabin feeders whose remaining margin the seat power candidate has already allocated to itself. Two offices were planning against the same number without either dossier saying so.
expected_findings.resolution: Extension held until the seat power allocation is fixed; the shared margin recorded on both work orders.

expected_findings.rationale: The conversion bulletin is written against three named operators and its cabin arrangement references are theirs. A fleet effectivity would need the arrangement references generalised, which is a re-write and not an amendment.
expected_findings.resolution: Bulletin left unchanged for the launch operators; no fleet effectivity issued.

type_data.conclusion: Rejected. The standard stays with its three launch operators until the carrier profile and the aft cabin feeder allocation are both resolved.
